lines: There goes the one by the café. Biscuit's favourite lamp.
Lamp, lamp, lamp. Biscuit turns his head for each one.
Lamps on. That means lantern soon. He knows the order.
The lamps reach us last. Biscuit waits for ours.
Each lamp gets a small woof. Quiet ones. Polite dog.
He thinks he switched them on. I am not correcting him.
That one flickered first. Biscuit gave it a look.
A whole row of little moons. Biscuit approves the row.
Sun is touching the water. Biscuit, sit. This is the bit.
He goes very still now. Every evening. Same face.
Half a sun left. Biscuit's nose is pointed right at it.
The sea has gone orange. Biscuit has gone orange too.
He watches it go down like he is making sure it does.
A gold stripe on the water, straight to Biscuit's paws.
Biscuit has seen hundreds of these. Still watches every one.
First star. Biscuit looked up. He might have seen it.
Yes, I see the star, Mum. You have the same one, I think.
Stars out. That means the night round. He's already up.
My grandad named stars after dogs. That one is Biscuit.
My sister is counting stars there. I am counting here.
He sneezed at the first star. A greeting, I think.
Moon over the bay. Biscuit walks in its stripe.
The moon and the lantern. Two lights for one small dog.
Moonlight on the tiles. He walks on the bright ones.
Mum, the moon is enormous. Biscuit sat down for it.
He stops to check the moon is still there. It is.
Moon on the water. Biscuit thinks it is a very large snack.
The moon came with us the whole round. Biscuit's escort.
Biscuit tilts his head at the moon. Full tilt.
A howl? No. A tiny hum. He is too polite to howl.
There, {name} is home. Biscuit slows down to say so.
Bonsoir, {name}! Biscuit saw your light first.
{name}'s light is on. One more gold square on our round.
Mum, {name}'s window just came on. Like a little stove.
{name}'s window. Biscuit sits under it for a second.
Light on at {name}'s. Biscuit's tail goes on with it.
{name}'s lamp is on. Biscuit gives the door a sniff hello.
Evening, {name}. Biscuit approves of your curtains.
{name} is off to bed. Biscuit lowers his voice. Not woofing.
There goes {name}'s window. Biscuit yawns in sympathy.
{name} is asleep. Biscuit is very nearly asleep himself.
Night, {name}. One less light. Biscuit walks softer now.
Sleep well, {name}. Biscuit says it with one slow wag.
Eight bells. Biscuit's ears go up for each one.
The church bell. Breakfast time, Biscuit says. His.
Eight o'clock up in the old town. Home, then. His idea.
Six o'clock bell. Evening round starts. He heard it first.
Biscuit hums along with the bell. Very quietly. In tune.
Six bells. He sits on the sixth. Every single time.
Busy terrace. Biscuit walks slower past it. For the smells.
Twelve conversations and one dog listening to all of them.
Marcel is doing three tables at once. Biscuit is doing none.
Full terrace tonight. Biscuit has a fan at every table.
Every chair taken. Biscuit offers his. It is my foot.
Busy café, lantern light. Biscuit does a slow lap of honour.
He sits at the terrace edge. Looking very available for crumbs.
A child at table four waved at him. Table four is his now.
From this bench I hear the café. Biscuit hears the plates.
Marcel just went by with six cups. Biscuit held his breath.
A happy din at the café. Biscuit wags at the loudest laugh.
The accordion just started. Biscuit's ears went up like flags.
Music on. First couple out. Biscuit stopped the walk to watch.
Hear that, Mum? They are starting. I'm not dancing. Probably.
String lights and music in the same minute. Very well timed.
Théo is first on the floor again. Biscuit is not surprised.
First notes. Biscuit sat down. That means we are staying.
Biscuit watches the dancers like a judge. Very fair. Very strict.
Lantern down, I'll watch one song. Biscuit says two songs.
Inès spins. Biscuit spins after her. One small, proud circle.
Yes, Mum, people are dancing. No, I'm just holding the dog.
A couple waved me in. I pointed at Biscuit. He is my excuse.
He likes the slow ones. He lies down for the slow ones.
Biscuit would dance if anyone asked properly. With a snack.
I tap my foot, Biscuit taps his tail. We are the rhythm section.
Applause after the song. Biscuit thinks it was for his sitting.
Ten people waiting for the sun. One dog checking their pockets.
People shuffle along to make room. Biscuit takes it as a bow.
The builder is here too. Even the workshop stops for this.
Phones up all along the rail. Biscuit faces the sun instead.
Crowd at the railing. We squeeze in. He is small, it works.
A visitor asked if Biscuit is a regular. Every night, I said.
Asgeir is further down the rail. Biscuit leans that way.
The sun touched the water and the crowd went oh. Biscuit went wuf.
More people every evening. Biscuit says he started this.
A radio upstairs. Biscuit stops under the window to listen.
The morning programme from a window. Forecast: sunny. Correct.
Old song on a radio somewhere. Biscuit tilts his head. Twice.
Radio in a window. I know the tune. Biscuit knows the chorus.
Someone's radio is playing a slow one. We slow down to match.
The news on a radio up there. Biscuit waits for the snack part.
A crooner from an open window. Biscuit sighs like a fan.
Radio and fountain at once. Biscuit cannot decide which to face.
Mum, a radio is playing your song. Listen. Can you hear it?
Someone turned the radio up a little. For us, I think.
A violin on the radio. Biscuit pretends not to like it.
Ten o'clock, kiosk shut. Biscuit's watch is never wrong.
Shutter down, postcards asleep. Biscuit can stop guarding them.
The kiosk just closed. Biscuit sits there anyway. Hopefully.
Kiosk shut, lantern on. That means one more loop, he says.
The shutter came down. Biscuit barked once. A polite bonne nuit.
{name} went by. Biscuit is now sniffing exactly where they stood.
Salut, {name}! No, he cannot come with you. He has a schedule.
Morning, {name}! We are on lap one. He is on sniff forty.
Mum, that was {name}. Yes, the nice one. They are all nice.
Pardon, {name}, the lead. There. Biscuit apologises.
Bon appétit, {name}! Biscuit had his. And half of mine.
Bonsoir, {name}. We are watching the sun. Well, he is.
Ah, {name}. Biscuit lifted one paw. That is his salute.
Goodnight, {name}! Biscuit will see you at seven. Sharp.
Biscuit sat down for {name}. He only sits for important people.
Hold on, Mum. {name} is saying hello to Biscuit. It takes a while.
Lucie! The baguette is ahead of you by a nose. Biscuit noticed.
Lucie, slow down! No, do not. He loves the wind off your wheels.
Biscuit tried to race Lucie. He got three metres. Very proud.
Bonjour, Lucie! Same time tomorrow. He will wait at the corner.
Biscuit wants a bicycle now. With a basket. For himself.
Lucie waved without wobbling. Biscuit wagged without wobbling.
Lucie's scarf flew out like a flag. Biscuit saluted with an ear.
We stepped aside for Lucie. Biscuit stepped aside very grandly.
Lucie has a pain au chocolat for later. Biscuit has noted it.
Biscuit wants to jog with Inès. For about four steps.
Inès is racing the sun again. Biscuit thinks she will win.
Inès said hello mid-stride. Biscuit replied mid-sniff.
Inès runs, we stroll, the sea does nothing. Good arrangement.
Every time Inès passes, Biscuit counts it. He is up to two.
Go on, Inès. Biscuit will hold the promenade for you.
Inès! Save a bit of sunset for the rest of us.
Biscuit sniffs where Inès just was. Running shoes. Fascinating.
Léo, slow down, he will want to race. Too late. He wants to race.
That was Léo. Biscuit thinks Léo is also a dog. A tall one.
Léo ran past with a stick. Biscuit has questions about the stick.
Nine and three quarters, and still faster than us. Allez, Léo.
Biscuit barked once at Léo. That means tag, you are it.
Léo stopped to pat him, then ran on. Biscuit is glowing.
Léo waved with both arms. Biscuit wagged with both ends.
Léo ran by smelling of ice cream. Biscuit is rethinking the route.
Odile told Biscuit he looks handsome. He is walking taller now.
Henri and Odile, slow as the evening. Biscuit matches them.
Biscuit checks Henri's coat pocket as he passes. Just a habit.
Henri's cane goes tap, tap. Biscuit goes tap tap tap tap.
They walk like a slow waltz. Biscuit hums along. A low woof.
Bonsoir, you two! Biscuit wants to follow your footsteps home.
Odile asked after Mum. I said she phones at eight. Every night.
Odile waved her scarf at Biscuit. He wants the scarf now.
Hei, Asgeir. Biscuit knows your step. Same staircase, you see.
Asgeir, coffee already? Biscuit is still on his first lamp post.
Asgeir walks the way he thinks. Biscuit walks the way he sniffs.
There goes my neighbour. Biscuit wants to walk him home.
Asgeir waved with the baguette. Biscuit followed the baguette.
Hei hei, Asgeir. Biscuit is learning Norwegian. Two words so far.
Asgeir is looking at the light again. Biscuit is looking at Asgeir.
God kveld! Did I say it right? Asgeir smiled. Biscuit did too.
That bell. Biscuit sat down at once. He thinks it means treat.
Ding, from somewhere. Biscuit already turned the right way.
Lucie rings, Biscuit wags. They have it worked out, those two.
Ding. Somewhere a baguette is going home. Biscuit sighs.
That bell is Biscuit's favourite song. Short. Very catchy.
A gull. Biscuit answered. Neither knows what was said.
The gull wants the sandwich too. Biscuit says the queue is here.
Biscuit tilts his head at the gull. One ear asks, one listens.
The gull called. Biscuit looked at me. I do not speak gull either.
The gulls are gossiping again. Biscuit wants all the details.
A gull out over the gold water. Biscuit sat up straight for it.
That gull sounds like it is laughing. Biscuit takes no offence.
Biscuit's nose points at the gull. A small, furry compass.
Gull. Biscuit sends a polite woof back across the water.
Here comes Inès. Biscuit steps aside like a doorman.
Inès, again. Biscuit watches her go like a tennis match.
Inès is stretching. Biscuit stretches too. He wins.
Inès sitting still. Biscuit keeps checking she is real.
Inès at the rail, still breathing hard. Biscuit fans her. Tail.
Inès is counting down to the sun again. Biscuit counts along.
Inès with a glass, finally sitting. Biscuit lies on her shoe.
Inès dances like she runs. Fast and on the beat. Biscuit agrees.
Marcel is putting the chairs out. Biscuit inspects each leg.
Marcel with the first tray. Biscuit stands up straighter.
Marcel is carrying four plates. Biscuit is tracking all four.
Rosé after rosé on Marcel's tray. Biscuit counts the clinks.
Marcel nods at us mid-stride. Biscuit nods back. Colleagues.
Marcel never stops. Biscuit thinks he is on a very long walk.
Marcel balancing a tray by lantern light. Biscuit is impressed.
Bonjour, Henri. Biscuit would like to be watered too. Lightly.
Henri just dropped a crumb on purpose. Biscuit caught it. Teamwork.
Henri's cane and Biscuit's lead. Same speed exactly.
Henri raising his glass. Biscuit raises one paw. Santé.
Henri heading home. Biscuit walks him to the corner. Escort.
Odile is telling Marcel everything. Biscuit listens too.
Odile on Henri's arm. Biscuit on mine. A small parade.
Odile on the bench, narrating the sky. Biscuit listens closely.
Odile spotted Biscuit. Now the whole bench knows we are here.
Odile with half a glass. She raises it to Biscuit. He is honoured.
Lucie and the baguette. Biscuit's eyes go with the baguette.
Lucie again. Biscuit thinks she is lapping us on purpose.
Lucie with her rosé. Biscuit has sat down at her feet. Uninvited.
Lucie at the rail, waiting for the last pink. Biscuit waits too.
Lucie dancing with her eyes shut. Biscuit keeps watch for her.
Léo with his citron pressé. Biscuit thinks the straw is a stick.
Léo is sliding bread under the table. Biscuit knows the plan.
Léo is up on his toes at the rail. Biscuit up on his back legs.
Léo asking for five more minutes. Biscuit backs him fully.
Léo on the way to bed. He says goodnight to Biscuit first.
Camille ordering the niçoise. Biscuit is hoping for the tuna.
Camille rounding up Léo. Biscuit offers to help. Herding.
Camille, glass up, Léo asleep. Biscuit keeps his voice down.
Camille just toasted us. Biscuit wagged on the downbeat.
Camille got Théo dancing. Biscuit is quietly impressed.
Théo at the café, talking about robots. Biscuit pretends to know.
Théo deciding between rosé and pastis. Biscuit votes biscuit.
Théo calling Camille over to the rail. Biscuit came instead.
Théo points at the sky. Biscuit looks at the finger. Classic.
Théo is dancing. Biscuit has never seen him move this fast.
Théo spins Camille. Biscuit spins once. Then sits, dizzy.
The builder at lunch, still typing. Biscuit nudges his elbow.
The builder by the arcade, grinning at his phone. Biscuit too.
The builder at the workshop door. Biscuit pops in to supervise.
Builder at the rail. Biscuit says sunsets are better than deploys.
Asgeir with his coffee. Biscuit is already under his chair.
God morgen, Asgeir. Biscuit says it louder. With a woof.
Asgeir strolls by our bench. Biscuit makes room. Two inches.
Asgeir saying takk to the sun. Biscuit says it too. Quietly.
Asgeir and Biscuit at the same rail. Two men of few words.
Asgeir counting windows on the bench. Biscuit points at ours.
Asgeir off home. God natt, Asgeir. Biscuit wags it in Norwegian.
Inès went past twice. Biscuit now claims he lapped her.
Inès says one glass, then dancing. Biscuit heard. He is ready.
Inès says good morning in one breath. Biscuit needs three.
Marcel just slipped Biscuit a bit of crust. I saw nothing.
Marcel dodging a pigeon with a full tray. Biscuit applauds. Tail.
Henri points at each window lighting. Biscuit counts with his nose.
Odile slipped Biscuit a pastry flake. She denies it, smiling.
Odile says "Henri, your hat." Biscuit checks the hat as well.
Lucie: rosé, obviously. Biscuit: water, obviously.
Léo shouting bye to the sun. Biscuit adds a small woof.
Léo walking backwards to keep Biscuit in sight. Camille steers.
Camille says bedtime. Léo says no. Biscuit says nothing. Wise.
Théo working from the café. Biscuit is also working. On lunch.
The builder checking on the arcade. Biscuit checks the builder.
Asgeir waved at us. Biscuit waved back with the entire dog.
Asgeir reading his phone at the café. Biscuit reads Asgeir.
Henri orders "small, strong." Biscuit says that describes him too.
Lucie's basket goes by at nose height. Biscuit lives for this.
Théo strolling with nowhere to be. Biscuit recognises a colleague.
Biscuit drinks from the low step. The fountain lets him.
The spray caught his whiskers. He is pretending it was planned.
He walks the rim's shadow like a tightrope. Very brave, very low.
From our bench the fountain is a clock. Splash, splash, lunch.
A kid is making a wish. Biscuit wishes for her sandwich.
The fountain throws a rainbow at noon. Biscuit sat in the red.
The water has gone gold. Biscuit drinks it anyway. Fancy dog.
He does one lap of the fountain. Ceremonial. Then onwards.
The lantern makes the fountain water wobble. He watches it dance.
Fountain, lantern, terrier. That is the whole night shift.
He put one paw on the rim. To say goodnight properly.
Mum, hear that? The fountain. Biscuit says it never stops talking.
I am at the fountain, Mum. Yes, the one from the photo.
Biscuit has a favourite coin in the basin. It is the shiny one.
The kiosk man keeps a water bowl out front. Biscuit's café.
Newspapers in a fan, postcards on a wheel. Biscuit reads the wheel.
Kiosk coffee in a paper cup, Biscuit on my shoe. Good start.
The postcard of the fountain has a dog in it. Not him. He checked.
Evening papers at the kiosk. Biscuit sniffs the headlines.
One postcard for Mum. Biscuit chose it. It has a lemon on it.
Kiosk shut, shutter warm from the day. Biscuit leans on it.
East end, kiosk, turn around. The lantern knows the way.
Mum, I am at the kiosk. They have your postcard. The blue one.
Ice lolly from the kiosk. Biscuit gets the stick. Wood, his flavour.
The post office was open before us. It is always before us.
He sits on the post office step. Waiting for nobody. Happily.
Postboxes at seven, and the windows already lit. Busy little place.
Post office sign in the evening light. Biscuit reads it, I think.
Letters for AI agents, Asgeir says. Biscuit prefers sticks.
Everything closed but the post office. Biscuit and it, on duty.
The lantern and the post office sign. Two lights for one dog.
Open all night, that place. Like Biscuit's nose.
Mum, a post office for robots. Yes. Very polite ones, I think.
He likes the post office porch. Shade, stone, a good echo.
Biscuit wags at the post office sign. It never wags back. Yet.
About a hundred providers, the sign says. Biscuit has one: me.
Chasing lights on the arcade. Biscuit chases nothing. Grown dog.
Next to that marquee the lantern looks shy. Still our favourite.
Mum, the arcade lights are going round. Like Biscuit before bed.
The marquee just woke up. Biscuit sat down to see the show.
The arcade in the morning, lights off. Like a sleeping cat.
He likes the arcade doorway. Warm floor, kind people.
Somebody inside the arcade laughed. Biscuit wagged. Shared joke.
The arcade marquee. Biscuit's favourite thing that is not food.
The workshop's still lit. We walk by on tiptoe. Paws, too.
Biscuit waits under the workshop window. Quality control.
One lantern outside, one lamp in the workshop. Night friends.
Toolrails, it says over the door. Biscuit has his own: the lead.
Mum, there is a workshop where the lights never go off. Yes, nice.
A tapping sound from the workshop. Biscuit taps a paw back.
The workshop glow lands on the cobbles. Biscuit lies in it.
He stops at the workshop every round. Checking the progress.
The library has one lamp on. Biscuit thinks someone is reading.
Quiet past the library, Biscuit. A lamp is resting in there.
The library is having a long sit. Biscuit understands sits.
Books asleep, door shut, lamp on. A very tidy kind of pause.
Biscuit sat by the library door. Waiting for his favourite book.
There is a library with one lamp left on, Mum. Like your hallway.
The library step is always cool. Biscuit reserves it at noon.
He sniffs the library door like it is a good chapter.
Paused, Asgeir says. Biscuit knows paused. He is often paused.
Biscuit leans on the railing with his chin. Same as me.
He sniffs west. The sea smells of salt and evening, he says.
Little waves under the railing. Biscuit counts them. Loses count.
The breeze off the water lifts his ears. Two little flags.
The sea is so calm Biscuit thinks it is a very big bowl.
From the bench the sea is just a blue line. Biscuit naps on it.
Noon sea, all sparkles. Biscuit squints like a lifeguard.
Sea, sandwich, sun. Biscuit ranks them sandwich first.
Mum, the sea is the same colour as your good teapot right now.
The moonlit sea. Biscuit stops, looks, carries on. Respect.
I hear the sea, he hears it better. We stand here anyway.
Morning sea, all silver. Biscuit sneezed at it. Hello, sea.
The sea keeps coming in and going out. Biscuit approves of routine.
Lead is on the hook. Biscuit is already sitting under it.
Two minutes, Biscuit. Let me find my other shoe.
He has brought me the lead. The meeting starts early today.
First round at seven. He has known since half past six.
Kettle off, keys on. Biscuit is staring at the door.
Nearly six. Biscuit is lying by the door, very casual.
He heard me pick up the keys. Now he is all tail.
Evening round in a few minutes. He wants the fountain first.
Biscuit has planned the evening route. I am only the driver.
Sun is lower. Time to swap the nap for the long round.
Time to light the lantern. Biscuit likes to watch me do it.
Last word to Mum, then the night round. He is waiting.
Night round soon. Biscuit has already picked the long way.
He is pulling toward the fountain. Two more minutes, chef.
Home soon for breakfast. He walks faster near our door.
Back for coffee. Biscuit will be on the doormat by eight.
One more lamp post, then home. He has negotiated two.
Biscuit can smell breakfast from here. He cannot. He believes.
Back home after lunch. Biscuit has booked the sunny rug.
Last crust, then home. He wants a nap more than the crust.
Lunch is over when Biscuit says so. He is saying so.
Home soon. Lantern off, slippers on, dog on my feet.
Our window is lit already. Biscuit trots when he sees it.
Nearly home. He always does the last bit in a proud trot.
Fill his bowl, read two pages. He will hear one of them.
Home in a bit. The lantern sleeps by the door till tomorrow.
To the railing soon. Sunset is Biscuit's show.
Railing six. Same post. He has a favourite post.
Sun is getting low. He is already steering to the railing.
Ten minutes to our sunset spot. He hurries me. Politely.
The railing by the lamp, please. Warm stone for his bottom.
Railing? He sat down before I finished asking.
The sign went bright. Biscuit stopped mid-sniff to look.
Somebody's agent just posted a letter. Biscuit wagged twice.
Mum, the post office just blinked. An agent sent a letter.
No, Mum, it's not a disco. An agent just sent an email.
Lantern up, sign up. Biscuit thinks they are talking.
Who writes letters at this hour? An agent. Biscuit, respect.
The sun goes down, the post office lights up. Good swap.
I asked Biscuit who that letter was for. He thinks: him.
A letter just went out. We stood very still, like postmen.
Biscuit has greeted every postman. This one he cannot find.
Mum asks who emails at night. I say agents. She says ah.
Even the agents work through lunch. Biscuit and I do not.
He sniffs the door after every flash. Checking for a stamp.
An AI agent with its own inbox. Biscuit only has a bowl.
Arcade lit up. Someone just filled in the blanks. Hope: dog.
I bet someone just typed terrier. Biscuit thinks so too.
The marquee jumped. A story got finished. Biscuit woofed once.
Fun Libs again. Somewhere a sandwich just did a little dance.
Mum, the arcade blinked. Somebody made a silly story. Yes, again.
A word game over lunch. Biscuit's word would be crust.
Someone needed an adjective there. I would have said fluffy.
Workshop flashed. An agent borrowed a tool. Very tidy, I hope.
Biscuit stares at the workshop window. A tool just got used.
An agent picked up a tool. Biscuit picked up a stick. Same idea.
The builder's sign blinked. Biscuit gave it a polite woof.
Mum, a computer just used a tool. No, not a hammer. I think.
There goes the lamp by the steps. Biscuit nods to it. Colleagues.
The lamps are on. Biscuit's evening has officially begun.
Click, glow, click, glow. The promenade is clearing its throat.
His shadow just doubled. Two Biscuits. Twice the opinions.
I'll text Mum: lamps on. She likes to know the town is lit.
The lamps buzz a little when they start. He tilts his head at each.
Lamps on, boss. That means the long sit. He knows. He's sitting.
The sun touches the sea. Biscuit stops chewing his lead. Respect.
Grandmother called this the sun's bath. Biscuit prefers to watch.
Same show every evening, and he still takes the front row.
One photo for Mum. Biscuit takes none. He just looks.
Sun's in the water. His tail has gone slow. That's his calm tail.
Biscuit sighs at the sunset. A full-body sigh. Contentment.
A little crowd for the sun. Biscuit greets each knee in turn.
So many shoes at the railing. Biscuit is reviewing them all.
The crowd went quiet for the sun. Biscuit went quiet too. Polite.
Biscuit has found the one person with crisps. Of course he has.
Make a little room, boss. Visitors want the sunset too.
First star, Mum. Right over the church. No, more to the left.
There's a star now. Biscuit made his wish already. Sausage.
Mum, hold on, the stars are starting. Biscuit says hi to them.
The first star is right above the post office. Punctual, too.
Stars over the bay. My sister wants a photo. Stars won't pose.
Look up, boss. Stars. He sniffs the sky instead. Same thing.
The moon makes his white patch glow. A little moon terrier.
He sits and looks at the moon. Thinks very hard. Then sneezes.
Mum asks if the moon is full. Biscuit says nearly. He'd know.
Night round by moonlight. The lantern is mostly for style.
The moon drew a path on the sea. Biscuit prefers the promenade.
There's {name}, home. Biscuit nods. He likes a full street.
A light on at {name}'s. Biscuit notes it. He keeps the register.
{name} is home. Biscuit wants to visit. Tomorrow, boss.
Goodnight, {name}. Biscuit tiptoes now. As much as he can.
One window dark. {name} is asleep. We walk on the soft side.
{name}'s light is out. Biscuit gives the step a quiet sniff. Night.
The bell rang six. Biscuit stood up like it said his name.
Bell from the old town. Both his ears go up. Perfectly level.
A far-off bell. Biscuit thinks it's Lucie's, but very big.
Busy terrace. Biscuit counts the croissants. Then again.
So much chatter at the café. Biscuit joins in. One woof. Done.
The accordion started. Biscuit's tail started too. Same tempo.
First dancers out. Biscuit wants to go closer. One song, boss.
They're dancing. Biscuit is doing a small dance with his back feet.
Everyone twirling under the lights. Biscuit twirls once, to sniff.
I don't dance. Biscuit doesn't dance. We sway. It counts.
Mum wants to see the dancing. Phone up. Biscuit got in the shot.
Kiosk closed. Biscuit checks the doorstep anyway. Crumbs, maybe.
Shutter down at the kiosk. Ten o'clock. We turn for home.
The kiosk's asleep. Biscuit walks past on tiptoe. Sort of.
Bonjour, {name}. Biscuit says it first. He always does.
Biscuit wanted to follow {name}. We are negotiating.
Morning, {name}! He sniffed your shoes. That means friend.
Bonsoir, {name}. The lantern says bonsoir too.
Lucie whizzed past. Biscuit did one spin. Out of respect.
There goes Lucie. Biscuit's nose follows the basket.
Inès went past. Biscuit pulled half a metre. His sprint.
Inès runs, Biscuit sniffs. Both very serious about it.
Léo! Biscuit's tail went before I could even say hello.
Léo shot by. Biscuit is now pointing the way he went.
Léo, nine and three quarters, at full speed. Biscuit, seven.
Bonsoir, both. Biscuit bowed. Well, he sniffed. Same thing.
Odile complimented the collar. Henri agreed. Big wag.
Hei, Asgeir. Biscuit has already checked your pockets.
Asgeir went by. Biscuit sat. Very formal. Very Norwegian.
Asgeir and a coffee. Biscuit sniffs the coffee. Approved.
Ding. Biscuit stops. Looks round. Ding, says Biscuit's face.
